question: What cost savings can a preventive maintenance program provide compared with a purely reactive program?
expected_answer: An estimated 12% to 18% on average.

question: What cost savings can a properly functioning predictive maintenance program provide over a program using preventive maintenance alone?
expected_answer: An estimated 8% to 12%.

question: According to the survey of companies using a CMMS, what was the average payback time?
expected_answer: 14.5 months (survey of 558 companies).

question: What do the letters OMETA stand for in O&M management?
expected_answer: Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Training, and Administration.

question: In what frequency range do the airborne ultrasounds detected by non-contact ultrasonic detectors fall?
expected_answer: 20 to 100 kHz.

question: How much does an infrared camera with full functionality cost?
Where should oil samples be taken for oil analysis?
expected_answer: From an active, low-pressure line, ahead of any filtration devices, and from the same place each time (a permanently installed sample valve is recommended).

question: What does the Karl Fischer test measure in oil analysis?
expected_answer: The amount of water in the lubricant.

question: What is the typical fee range of a new building commissioning provider per square foot?
expected_answer: From $0.50/ft2 for simple buildings to $3.00/ft2 for complex buildings such as hospitals and laboratories.

question: What are the four predominant levels of resource metering?
expected_answer: One-time/spot measurement, run-time measurement, short-term monitoring, and long-term monitoring.

question: What minimum annual savings percentage should Federal sites use when evaluating whether a meter is cost-justified?
expected_answer: A minimum of 2 percent annual savings.

question: How often should machines with motors of 7.5 hp or larger be evaluated for routine lubricating oil analysis?
expected_answer: From monthly to quarterly (hydraulic systems, except mobile systems, quarterly).

question: How does the annual cost per horsepower of reactive maintenance compare with that of reliability centered maintenance?
expected_answer: Reactive maintenance costs about $18/hp/yr, RCM about $6/hp/yr: RCM costs about one third, $12/hp/yr less.

question: What share of maintenance is reactive in an average facility compared with continually top-performing facilities?
expected_answer: More than 55% in an average facility versus less than 10% in top-performing facilities.

question: What steam trap failure rates are reported in the infrared thermography section and in the ultrasonic analysis section?
expected_answer: Thermography section: without a good program, 15% to 60% of traps can be failed open. Ultrasound section: initial surveys in the petrochemical industry found 34% of traps had failed, mostly open.

question: Would the annual savings from the compressed air leak case study at the northeast plant cover the cost of a typical ultrasonic scanner?
expected_answer: Yes. A typical handheld ultrasonic scanner costs $750 to $10,000, and correcting the leaks saved the plant $13,000 per year (plus avoiding a $50,000 compressor).

question: Which two technologies described in the guide can give an indication of bearing wear, and how?
expected_answer: Ultrasound: a 12-50x increase in amplitude at 28-32 kHz gives early indication of bearing deterioration. Infrared thermography: trended IR scans of bearings (hot bearings) indicate wear.

question: What examples does the guide give of extending oil change intervals by using the actual oil condition instead of a fixed schedule?
expected_answer: Any of these examples from the guide: (1) car: instead of changing oil every 3,000-5,000 miles, oil analysis could extend the change to 10,000 miles; (2) a northeast industrial facility gained an average of 0.5 years between oil changes, saving more than $20,000 in consumables in less than 9 months; (3) a major northeast manufacturer switched 400 machines to condition-based oil changes, saving more than $54,000 per year. A correct answer gives at least two of these examples.

question: How does the cost of a full-function infrared camera compare with a high-end vibration analyzer?
expected_answer: A full-function IR camera costs $18,000 to $65,000; a high-end vibration analyzer with software and accessories can exceed $30,000.

question: Was the payback of the EMSL recommissioning project at PNNL consistent with typical recommissioning paybacks reported in the guide?
expected_answer: Yes. EMSL invested about $125,000 and saved $173,735 per year (payback well under 1 year); typical recommissioning paybacks are usually under 2 years and often under 0.5 year.

question: What payback periods does the guide give for infrared thermography equipment and for high-end vibration analysis equipment?
expected_answer: Infrared: on average 12 months or less. High-end vibration equipment: a typical industrial site can recover the cost within 2 years.
